### T. J. Stevenson & Co. and Irving Trust Company v. Janis Transportation Company — Dispute over Recovery of Advanced Crew Wages and Vessel Expenses and Enforcement of Ship Mortgage Rights

Plaintiff: T. J. Stevenson & Co., USA.
Address: 15 John Street, New York, United States of America.
Legal Representative: Thomas Stevenson Jr., General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Shen Zhenguo, Attorney at Shanghai International Economic and Trade Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Tang Yilin, Attorney at Shanghai International Economic and Trade Law Firm.

Plaintiff: Irving Trust Company, USA.
Address: 1 Wall Street, New York, United States of America.
Legal Representative: Limon Gibbon, Vice President of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Yin Dongnian, Attorney at Shanghai Maritime Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Tao Yong, Graduate Student of Shanghai Maritime University.

Defendant: Janis Transportation Company.
Address: 80 Broad Street, Monrovia, Republic of Liberia.
Legal Representative: Li Fuping, President of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Tang Zuqian, Attorney at Shanghai Maritime Law Firm.

On November 4, 1985, Plaintiff T. J. Stevenson & Co. filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai Maritime Court on the grounds that the Defendant Janis Transportation Company failed to fulfill its obligations as shipowner and did not reimburse the Plaintiff for the crew wages and other expenses advanced by the Plaintiff on behalf of the Defendant's vessel "Opal City" (hereinafter referred to as the "Opal City"). The Plaintiff alleged: The crew wages advanced for the Opal City and various vessel expenses incurred during the vessel's detention at Whyalla, Australia, totaling $396,134.25, constitute a priority claim, and requested the compulsory sale of the Opal City to satisfy the above debts.

On December 12, 1985, Plaintiff Irving Trust Company filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai Maritime Court on the grounds that the Defendant failed to perform the ship mortgage contract and defaulted on a loan principal and interest of USD 6.8 million, requesting the sale of the Defendant's mortgaged vessel Opal City and priority satisfaction of the mortgage debt owed to the Defendant.

During the proceedings, the Defendant did not file a defense but later, on May 31, 1986, sent a letter to the Shanghai Maritime Court, explicitly stating that it did not contest the authenticity and completeness of the USD 6.8 million debt claim asserted by Plaintiff Irving Trust Company.

After accepting the case, the Shanghai Maritime Court reviewed it and concluded that the subject matters of the two Plaintiffs' claims were common and should constitute a joint action, and that the cases could be consolidated for trial pursuant to Article 47, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation).

The Shanghai Maritime Lawfully formed a collegial panel and, after a public hearing, found the following facts:

On February 27, 1981, Pelion Great Transport Company, Liberia, using its Liberian-flagged vessel "Opal Star" as collateral, borrowed USD 8.15 million from Irving Trust Company in New York, USA. On the same day, the parties registered the mortgage at the office of the Liberian Maritime Commission located in New York, USA, and executed corresponding mortgage documents for the agreed priority ship mortgage. The mortgage documents stated that if Pelion Great Transport Company breached the mortgage contract, Irving Trust Company had the right to declare all outstanding loan principal immediately due and payable, demand repayment of principal and accrued interest in full, and exercise the rights conferred on Irving Trust Company as a mortgage creditor under Liberian maritime law or any other applicable law. Subsequently, the vessel "Opal Star" was renamed "Opal City".

On October 4, 1984, Irving Trust Company and Pelion Great Transport Company transferred the Opal City and the rights and obligations under the priority ship mortgage to the Defendant, Janis Transportation Company, and executed a transfer contract. The contract stated that Irving Trust Company, as the mortgage creditor of the Opal City, agreed to Pelion Great Transport Company's transfer of all rights and obligations under the ship and the priority ship mortgage to Janis Transportation Company. Upon acquiring ownership of the vessel, Janis Transportation Company replaced Pelion Great Transport Company as the mortgage debtor of the vessel and assumed and enjoyed all rights and obligations of a mortgage debtor. On the same day, the mortgage particulars recorded in the Opal City's certificate of registry were correspondingly amended and registered at the office of the Liberian Maritime Commission in New York, USA.

Thereafter, East Asia Co., Ltd., Denmark, entered into a 24-month time charter party with the Defendant for the Opal City. The charter party provided that East Asia Co., Ltd. had the right to sub-charter the Opal City during the charter period. On July 3, 1985, East Asia Co., Ltd. entered into a charter party of approximately 60 days with Plaintiff T. J. Stevenson & Co. On July 12 of the same month, the Opal City arrived at the port of Whyalla, Australia.

In March 1985, China National Metals and Minerals Import and Export Corporation (hereinafter referred to as China Minmetals) entered into a contract with Baoqin Mountain Co., Ltd., Australia, for the purchase and sale of 20,000 metric tons of steel billets. China Minmetals commissioned American Minerals Co., Ltd. to charter the Opal City from T. J. Stevenson & Co. The Opal City loaded 19,999.527 metric tons of steel billets at Whyalla on July 15 of that year. On July 24, the Opal City issued a bill of lading. After loading, due to the Defendant's default in paying crew wages, the crew refused to sail, causing the Opal City to be detained for an extended period. During this time, the master of the Opal City repeatedly contacted the Defendant but received no substantive response, and thus turned to T. J. Stevenson & Co. for assistance. To complete the vessel's scheduled voyage, T. J. Stevenson & Co. reached an agreement with the crew of the Opal City on September 27 of that year: it agreed to advance crew wages and crew repatriation costs of USD 229,653, covering the period up to and including October 31 of the same year. The master and crew of the Opal City simultaneously assigned their maritime claims and other rights and interests to T. J. Stevenson & Co.

In addition, T. J. Stevenson & Co. also claimed to have advanced other expenses incurred by the Opal City due to the detention, amounting to USD 166,481.20, but failed to provide valid evidence.

On September 5, 1985, Irving Trust Company, because the Defendant failed to fulfill its obligations as a mortgage debtor, sent a letter to the Defendant demanding immediate repayment of the matured loan principal and interest of USD 6.8 million, but the Defendant did not repay. The Opal City departed from Whyalla, Australia on September 29, 1985, and arrived at the port of Shanghai, China in mid-October. The above facts are confirmed by evidence including the ship mortgage documents, the mortgage transfer contract, the loan contract, the certificate of registry, the master's report, and the crew's assignment of rights agreement, which were not disputed by the Plaintiffs and the Defendant.

On October 30 of the same year, all crew members of the Opal City applied to the Shanghai Maritime Court for permission to leave the vessel, on the grounds that the crew wages advanced by the Plaintiff only covered up to October 31. On November 1, the Shanghai Maritime Court lawfully granted the crew's application to leave the vessel and appointed personnel to guard the vessel. When the master of the Opal City left the vessel, he submitted to the Shanghai Maritime Court the vessel's spare cash of USD 2,630.50 and A$658.20.

After Plaintiff T. J. Stevenson & Co. filed an application for pre-litigation preservation on October 19, 1985, the Shanghai Maritime Court, on October 30, lawfully ruled to order the Defendant to provide a cash guarantee of USD 480,000 within 5 days; failing to provide the guarantee within that time would result in the attachment of the Opal City. After 5 days passed, the Defendant did not provide the guarantee. On November 5, the Shanghai Maritime Court lawfully ruled to attach the vessel and issued an attachment order, attaching the Opal City in the port of Shanghai. Thereafter, the Defendant still did not provide a guarantee. On December 11, the court ruled to sell the Opal City and issued a public notice for the auction of the vessel.

On January 17, 1986, the Shanghai Maritime Court lawfully publicly auctioned the Opal City, which was purchased by the highest bidder, Irving Trust Company, for USD 1,301,000, with a deposit of USD 400,000 paid on the spot. After the Shanghai Maritime Court issued the public notice for the sale of the Opal City, Baoqin Mountain Co., Ltd., Australia, on the grounds that the detention of the Opal City caused it to incur additional shifting fees and berth occupancy fees totaling A$43,430; American Minerals and Metals Company, on the grounds that the Defendant's delay in delivery caused loan interest losses and additional expenses such as berth occupancy for the Opal City totaling USD 299,603.52; and the American Bureau of Shipping, on the grounds that the Opal City owed classification survey fees of USD 23,166, each filed applications for registration of their claims. When these claimants learned that they would receive no actual recovery according to the order of satisfaction, they withdrew their claims.

The Shanghai Maritime Court held that: The Defendant, as the owner of the Opal City, failed to fulfill its duties by defaulting on crew wages for a long period, causing the vessel to be detained at Whyalla. The claim by Plaintiff T. J. Stevenson & Co. for advancing crew wages and repatriation costs of USD 229,653 to enable the vessel to complete its scheduled voyage and deliver the loaded cargo to the port of destination constitutes a priority claim. In accordance with international practice, this claim shall be satisfied by priority from the proceeds of the sale of the Defendant's vessel Opal City. The claim by T. J. Stevenson & Co. for reimbursement of other expenses allegedly advanced on behalf of the Defendant due to the detention of the Opal City is not supported due to lack of valid evidence.

The ship mortgage contract concluded between Plaintiff Irving Trust Company and the Defendant, having been registered with the relevant authorities under the laws of the Republic of Liberia, has legal effect. The Defendant breached the provisions of the mortgage contract by defaulting for a long period on the loan principal and interest of USD 6.8 million owed to the Plaintiff, and shall bear full liability for repayment. In accordance with international practice, the law of the flag state shall be applied. Under the laws of the Republic of Liberia, a mortgage constitutes a priority claim against the mortgaged vessel to the extent of the secured obligations.

The expenses incurred by the Shanghai Maritime Court in connection with the attachment and sale of the Opal City, totaling USD 143,725.02, shall be deducted first from the proceeds of the sale of the vessel.

In summary, both Plaintiffs are entitled to priority satisfaction from the proceeds of the sale of the Opal City and any interest thereon, after deducting the court's litigation costs and expenses incurred in the attachment and sale of the vessel. The spare cash of the Opal City shall also be used for satisfaction.

On the basis of ascertaining the facts and clarifying the liabilities, the Shanghai Maritime Court, pursuant to Article 97 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), presided over mediation on October 7, 1987, and the two Plaintiffs and the Defendant reached the following agreement through consultation:

From the proceeds of the sale of the Opal City amounting to USD 1,301,000 and the interest accrued on the deposit paid by the vessel's purchaser totaling USD 12,815.92, plus the spare cash of the Opal City of USD 2,630.50 and A$658.20, after deducting various expenses for the attachment and sale of the vessel of USD 143,725.02, the remaining amount of USD 1,172,721.40 and A$658.20 shall be distributed as follows: Plaintiff T. J. Stevenson & Co. receives USD 292,000.00 and A$658.20; Plaintiff Irving Trust Company receives USD 880,721.40.

The court acceptance fee of RMB 31,631.45 and other expenses of RMB 1,553.00 shall be borne by Plaintiff T. J. Stevenson & Co. in the amount of RMB 7,345.00 and by Plaintiff Irving Trust Company in the amount of RMB 25,839.45.
